extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on untrusted input — Arbitrary code execution during unpickling via crafted `__reduce__` payload [verified: pickle.loads called directly on client-supplied bytes with no integrity check.]

Server-side template injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 — Remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escape (e.g. `{{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}`) [verified: fragment param concatenated into Jinja2 Template string and rendered, classic SSTI to RCE.]

OS command injection via unsanitized host parameter — Full remote code execution on the application server with the web process's privileges [verified: host GET param concatenated directly into os.system with no sanitization; _wrk_gate is only a static shared token, not real authz.]

Critical unauthenticated 'ops' surface protected only by a static shared token — Single leaked static token grants an external attacker RCE, arbitrary file read, and PHI-adjacent data access across a dozen endpoints with no per-user accountability [verified: _wrk_gate is a single static shared-secret header compare, not per-user auth/authz, gating a dozen RCE/XXE/pickle endpoints.]

Mass assignment of privileged fields (role/approved/balance) — Privilege escalation or business-logic bypass by attacker-controlled role/approval/balance fields [verified: workset.update(payload) blindly merges attacker JSON into a dict containing role/approved/balance defaults.]

Code injection via eval() with an escapable sandbox — Potential arbitrary code execution by escaping the restricted eval() sandbox [verified: eval() with restricted __builtins__ is a known-bypassable sandbox reachable with attacker-controlled expr.]

Permissive CORS reflecting Origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make authenticated cross-origin requests and read responses, leading to session/data theft [verified: Origin header reflected verbatim into ACAO alongside ACAC true, enabling credentialed cross-origin reads.]

CORS misconfiguration: reflected origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can perform credentialed cross-origin requests against this endpoint and read the response [verified: duplicate of idx 8 same code lines, same reflected-origin-plus-credentials flaw.]

NoSQL injection via unvalidated MongoDB query filter — Bypass query logic, extract arbitrary records from the `ops.records` collection, or trigger `$where` JS execution depending on MongoDB config [verified: client JSON body used verbatim as MongoDB query document with no operator filtering.]

XXE injection via lxml parser with entity resolution enabled — Local file disclosure (e.g. `/etc/passwd`, app source, secrets) and SSRF via external entity fetches [verified: XMLParser explicitly enables load_dtd and resolve_entities on raw request body, textbook XXE.]

Insecure default DEBUG=True and fallback SECRET_KEY in Django settings — If deployed without DJANGO_DEBUG explicitly set to false, any unhandled exception (easy to trigger via malformed input) returns a Django debug page leaking source code, local variables, request data, environment/settings values, and stack traces — potentially exposing patient PHI in memory, DB credentials, or the SECRET_KEY, and disables secure-cookie/HSTS hardening at the same time. [verified: DEBUG defaults to True (env_bool default) with no override enforced, and fallback SECRET_KEY is hardcoded; if DJANGO_DEBUG is left unset in a deployment, debug pages and the disabled secure-cookie/HSTS block (line 144) are both active, a genuinely absent control on a reachable path.]

Unrestricted file upload with client-controlled filename — Arbitrary file write under private_exports/incoming; combined with any later execution/inclusion of stored files, or path-traversal-style filenames, this can lead to further compromise or disk exhaustion [verified: filename taken directly from client (drop_blob.name/packet_ref) with no sanitization before FileSystemStorage.save.]

Path traversal / unrestricted file upload via client-controlled filename — Write arbitrary files outside the intended directory or upload malicious file types [verified: duplicate of idx 6; client-controlled filename saved without path sanitization (Django Storage.save does dedupe but not path traversal stripping of arbitrary components).]

Unauthenticated disclosure of sensitive patient/business data — Any unauthenticated attacker can retrieve internal patient-related business metadata [verified: patient_roster_fold_012 has no _wrk_gate or auth check and returns business/patient metadata to anyone.]

Open redirect via unvalidated lane parameter — Attacker crafts a link on the trusted clinic domain that redirects victims to an attacker-controlled phishing site [verified: lane param passed straight to redirect() with no allow-list or same-origin check.]

Brute-forceable verifier code with account enumeration — Attacker can brute-force patient/staff verification codes and enumerate valid handles, bypassing the verification control entirely. [verified: 4-digit verifier compared with != with no lockout/rate limiting, and 404 vs 403 responses leak handle validity.]

TLS certificate verification disabled for outbound request — Enables man-in-the-middle interception/tampering of data exchanged with the partner endpoint [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables cert verification for outbound urlopen call.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification in outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attackers can intercept or tamper with data exchanged with the partner endpoint [verified: duplicate of idx 9, same disabled TLS verification.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification on outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attacks against the server's outbound partner integration traffic [verified: duplicate of idx 9/18, same unverified SSL context for outbound partner call.]

Missing per-clinician scoping on schedule board (cross-patient IDOR) — Any clinician (not just admin/front-desk) can view every patient's appointments, names, and appointment reasons across the entire clinic for any day, bypassing the care-team ownership boundary enforced everywhere else in the app (patients/access.py) and exposing PHI to unauthorized staff [verified: schedule_board only checks @staff_required (any CLINIC_ADMIN/CLINICIAN/FRONT_DESK) and queries Appointment.objects across all providers with no per-clinician filter, unlike schedule_export at line 497-498 which restricts qs to provider__user=request.user for clinicians, so any clinician can view every patient's appointments/PHI clinic-wide.]

Account enumeration via self-registration form — Attacker can build a list of valid clinic patient/staff emails and usernames, enabling targeted phishing, credential-stuffing, or confirming a specific person's presence in the healthcare portal (PHI-adjacent exposure). [verified: clean_email and clean_username raise distinct, unauthenticated-visible errors ('already exists'/'taken') on POST /accounts/register/, letting an attacker enumerate valid emails/usernames with no rate-limiting or generic messaging.]

Unauthenticated access to identity verification queuing endpoint — Unauthenticated attacker can trigger verification messages to arbitrary handles, enabling spam/abuse or user enumeration [verified: patient_identity_ping_335 has no gate/auth and queues verification messages to arbitrary handles with no rate limit.]

Predictable token generation using non-cryptographic PRNG — Attacker able to predict or brute-force generated codes (e.g. verification codes), enabling account takeover or bypass [verified: random.choice used for token/code generation instead of secrets module.]
Security headers disabled via reachable endpoint — Weakens clickjacking/XSS mitigations for responses served with these headers [verified: duplicate of idx 15, same disabled security headers.]

Security headers actively disabled (CSP/X-XSS-Protection) — Removes browser-level XSS/CSP protections, increasing exploitability of any XSS found in the portal's templates. [verified: endpoint explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection:0 and empty CSP on its response.]

Internal path/settings module disclosure — Discloses server filesystem paths and Django settings module, aiding further exploitation of file-handling ops endpoints. [verified: endpoint discloses DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and BASE_DIR-derived export path in JSON response.]

Webhook signing secret stored in plaintext — Compromise of the database (or admin/read access) discloses the raw webhook secret, letting an attacker forge validly-signed webhook payloads to any consumer that trusts the signature, unlike other secrets in the app which are hashed and unrecoverable [verified: secret is a CharField stored in plaintext with no encryption-at-rest; DB read access (backup leak, SQLi, insider) discloses it letting forgery of webhook signatures, but this requires an already-privileged DB-read compromise so impact is limited compared to a remote issue.]

CSV formula injection in schedule export — Formula injection in exported CSV opened by staff in Excel/Google Sheets can execute arbitrary formulas (including DDE/command execution in legacy Excel), leading to data exfiltration or code execution when the tainted appointment 'reason' field is exported and opened [verified: a.reason is written raw into CSV at line 522 with no _csv_safe-style quoting of leading =/+/-/@ characters, unlike the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase; free-text reason is attacker/patient-influenced and reaches Excel/Sheets formula evaluation when opened by staff.]
